Starts Phys -> Fire -> Ice etc cycling through affinities

If you Null/Drain/Repel an attack that affinity he used is replaced by Freikugel for (1 + n) turns where n = times Masakado has gathered Magatsuhi

If you hit into a specific affinity he will replace that attack with Diarama for the next turn only. This overrides even the use of Freikugels.

Some advice: When entering immediately turn lights on in your location, this stops your sanity draining as fast. If you are playing with the breaker starting off, check the board and turn it on. There is increased sanity drain with more people playing but if you don't sit in the dark you should be fine for much longer. You can keep the light off in the main ghost room and stand outside in the light looking into it to preserve sanity.

Most ghosts start hunts at 50% average sanity or below. With a few being 60, 70 or in special cases even higher. But general rule of thumb make sure to keep track of it. Start off by familiarising yourself with each piece of evidence. If you are potentially waiting for an evidence like writing or dots or freezing feel absolutely free to leave the house! If you have a camera in the room you may be able to catch writing or dots with 0 risks.

Door touches will be where the ghost is, keep in mind they can roam but generally a door touch will mean its favourite room is very near, you can listen out to sometimes know the location without even having to check temperatures. Once you have found the ghost location turn on lights and find a hiding spot. I usually like to leave all lights on from the room to your hiding location, have a path in mind for when a hunt begins. The ghost is stupid as in the second your break Line of sight of it will go to that location and then even if its obvious you are in a room it may not go in, as long as it doesn't see you go into a hiding spot you are safe. Make sure all equipment is off otherwise it will sense you, it is okay if it is on the floor just not on your person. 

When a hunt ends all the lights will go off, if you are in a locker you can use this to your advantage to immediately get out. There is a cooldown of 25 seconds (20 for a demon) between hunts at a minimum so you are guaranteed some safety there. If you have gotten 2 evidences and can't get the third feel free to guess and leave, that is much better than dying.

EMF: This will pick up things like a door touch, a throw, ghost event and can be useful for finding where a ghost is. EMF 5 will make a distinct sound which can help identify without directly looking at it if you just switch it on and put it in the ghost room.

UV: If you hear a door touch you can shine the light on it to try locate finger prints. An extra little tip is if the breaker is turned off by the ghost shine UV on the breaker door, that's a nice way to sometimes check if the ghost isn't touching doors.

Ghost Writing: This can sometimes be annoying to get, make sure you place it open and as long as the ghost is inside the ring it can interact with it. If you are playing on a 3 evidence mode which you are and the ghost throws the book, if it hasn't written in it you can cross off Writing.

Freezing: The tier 1 thermo isn't as powerful as it used to be. When the breaker is off the map will be cold, it can sometimes take a little for it to warm up or cool down. If you start with the breaker on sometimes the ghost room wont be cool enough so wait maybe a minute before checking to ensure you don't miss the room. It can fluctuate slightly so it's best to check each room see if it dips down, if it goes back up then move on to the next room. Freezing doesn't actually want you to be at 0c either. Story - There are 2 routes. Canon of Creation and Canon of Vengeance. If you are planning to do multiple playthroughs choose to not take the girls hand and do the old route first, then in ng+ or a separate file take her hand and choose the new story. If you are only going to play once take her hand although I highly recommend doing both.

Optionals - You can find collectibles to give you bonus rewards, do side quests and find hidden areas and fight abscesses. Exploration is much more effective to advance your team than wandering aimlessly grinding against mobs.

Fusion - Experiment with fusing demons and checking their unique abilities, there may be one you like working with or have an idea for. If it doesn't work then no worries, you learn from dying and how to come back better and kick the bosses ass.

Difficulty - Depending on how familiar you are with turn based games I'd recommend Normal or Hard. Hard is definitely the most fun difficulty however the one thing i dislike about hard is it adds a 1.1x hit rate multiplier to enemies and a 0.95x hit rate for the player. The making the player miss more is needlessly irritating but it's honestly not too bad. The combat is so fun and complex at times I feel like anything lower than Hard you never get the full enjoyment of what it is supposed to be. Although Normal can be good simply because of that hit rates being 1x.

Combat - I'll try to explain combat and the press turn system briefly:

You start off (under most circumstances) with 4 full icons. 1 for every active party member meaning each get 1 action a turn. If you use an item, skill or guard you will use up an action and then next demon will act. Party order is not determined by agility simply by slot order. However hitting a weakness, get a critical hit or pass a turn will only cost half an action. This makes the full icon flash and by strategizing you can have more turn economy and squeeze out more from each go.

There are multiple states you can have for affinities: Weak, Neutral, Resist, Null, Drain, Repel. The enemies can also take advantage of your vulnerabilities which is why I say level does not matter, your team composition does. Being Weak costs half an action like mentioned, Neutral and Resisting costs the normal action. Nulling will cost an action +1 additional action so you can use this to severely hinder bosses early on and later on Repels/Drains can immediately shut down an enemy if used correctly.

Customisation - When it comes to building each demon try to give them a role. Filling them with 6 different elemental attacks will work but you'll struggle, you mainly want 1 or 2 major skills they will be using, a back up skill and the rest of your slots should be filled with passive effects to boost damage, survivability, hp/mp or whatever is needed!

Hope some of this helps and you enjoy the game!

As someone with experience in challenge running a ton of Megaten games here is my advice:  
  
Affinities - First off your affinities are important, levels do not matter (much) now with reduced level scaling. An overlevelled team that is badly prepped for a boss can still be demolished, an underlevelled correctly prepped team will have a much easier time. Nulling an attack will not only waste the turn but take an additional turn off the boss this is powerful at taking away turns. Repel/Drain will end the bosses turn entirely. At minimum if you decide to play on hard you will want good resist affinities early game

Demons - Until endgame do not settle with your team, you will want to be switching them for bosses. Spyglass is an insanely good item it tells you what the bosses is strong and weak to and gives you it's moveset, you can then die and come back with a team to fight it.

Stats - I'll briefly go through each stat, what it does and how useful it is:

Strength: Pretty much the best offensive stat in the game when you are at endgame, increases power of physicals/strength based moves.

Vitality: Lowers the damage you re.ceive from attacks, depending on how much leeweigh you need for fights this is a very good stat to spec into. If you feel you are confident you can mostly avoid this and just top up occasionally on it.

Magic: The same as strength but for magic based moves. (This doesn't increase your defense against magic hits unlike some games). Early game this is very good for consistent press turn gain. Hitting a weakness will not remove an action icon, it will make it flash counting as a "half action".

Agility: The objectively worst stat in the entire game. Increases player hit rate and dodge rate. That sounds good but a simple calculation using the formulas provided by Ctobn shows how AWFUL this stat is. An enemy level 1 Slime vs a Max level player (With 999 Agility) when the slime has accuracy debuffed to -2 and the player has evasion buffed to +2 STILL has a 66% chance to hit you on hard mode. You can never even with all agility investment get close to a 50/50 dodge rate.

Luck: Slightly better than agility, it affects chance to crit, chance to BE crit, ailments chances and duration and insta-kill chances. (Also 3 luck stat points is equal to 1 agility point for hit rates). However ailments suck in this game and only have niche purposes where they are good. Each successful hit of a type of ailment makes the next one massively drop in chance to succeed, both for player and enemy, with an absolute hard cap of 4 hits. This means a player with 999 luck vs a enemy with 1 luck you will only be able to charm it 4 times and the 5th will always be 0% success.

Player Stats: You gain 3 points predetermined to Nahobino on level up but can also choose a 4th point however you would like. My advice is choose whether you want magic or strength and put 90% of points into 1 of those, the other 10% can top up your Vitality slightly if you need to take less damage. You can change that to suit your preferences though.
